items.author: Ben
items.title: The profitability ledger - the whole field's filed returns, one row per corporation
items.design:
The surface for BL-626 (quarterly return) and the host of the buyout press. DESIGN-OWED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by omission: its question_log.json pair - the question it answers, why it earns its space, the item that demanded it - is required on every surface and its wording is Ben's. What is already settled: a table, one row per corporation, refreshed each quarter; exact figures where the firm files and a dash where it does not (FINANCE.md § Disclosure); no bands anywhere. Open: which rail slot it takes, and whether it absorbs the financial half of the slot-8 Corporations table (docs/ui/ledgers/corporation.md carries that as its own open question).

BEN ANSWERED BOTH OPEN QUESTIONS, 2026-08-29, describing the new acquisitions ledger: "This ledger should have a fold out option which displays a full table, sortable by type, end resource, input resource, profit... And any other useful fields."

SO: (1) it takes NO rail slot of its own - it is the FOLD-OUT of BL-675 (acquisitions ledger), reached by the BL-214 full-canvas disclosure control the Corporation dashboard already uses. (2) It DOES absorb the financial half of the slot-8 Corporations table: BL-674 strips Reach and Share from that surface, and this table is where the per-firm financial read now lives. docs/ui/ledgers/corporation.md carried both as its own open questions; both are now closed and the doc should say so.

COLUMNS, from Ben's list plus what the feed already holds: type, end resource (the recipe's output), input resource, profit (the filed net - BL-626's quarterly return, and the trailing mean the price is read off), price, and ownership class. Sortable on each. Exact where the firm files, a dash where it does not, no bands (FINANCE.md § Disclosure).

STILL OWED AND STILL BEN'S: the question_log.json pair. Every surface carries the question it answers and why it earns its space, and that wording is his - the item cannot close without it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Rivals buy firms too - buy_corporation joins the scored-utility candidate list
items.design: The symmetry half of BL-628 (whole-firm buyout), and a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in its established shape: deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, a legal verb and never a planner. THE WORK: score buy_corporation in corp_ai.cpp's existing candidate list, capped at one acquisition per evaluation, its price carried in the candidate's spend under the solvency gate so a rival cannot buy itself below its reserve floor. Availability is gated on the target's ownership class, not on the acquirer's cash - the 'never on cash' ruling's shape. Record the grant in the standing rules with its date, as every prior widening is recorded. SAVING UP IS NOT PLANNING, and this item owns the distinction: Ben's Sprint 20 goal wants a corp to accumulate cash toward an acquisition, but a scorer that defers a cheap build today in order to afford a firm tomorrow is edging toward the planner the standing rules forbid. The honest route needs no new machinery - accumulation is EMERGENT when the buy candidate outscores the marginal build, since a tick with no affordable positive candidate simply banks its cash. Whether that actually happens at the authored weights is a measurement, and BL-634 (acquisition viability) is where it is taken.

THE WORK: re-budget the columns against shell_column_width(disp.x) rather than fixed pixels, and decide whether the stance presses belong in-row at this width at all or behind the row's Selection drill. items.author: Ben
items.title: Construction draws materials - in the opening years, and as centres grow
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'we need those first 20 years of generation to include construction'. MEASURED CONTEXT: materials are authored per building (resource_costs) and charged at the build press, but generation PLACES buildings rather than constructing them, so the draw never fires during the opening years - stone and timber have a construction sink on paper and no pull in practice. TWO HALVES, and the second is the one that lasts: (1) make the opening years actually build, so the warm start carries a real material pull; (2) make POPULATION CENTRES draw construction materials as they grow, which does not decay once the warm start ends. An ancient economy's largest material sink is building, and half (2) makes that structurally true rather than transiently.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Roads, ports and hubs draw materials to stay standing
items.design: The infrastructure demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). The logistics_maintenance budget line already exists and names exactly this, so the state half has a home. THE WORK: a network that consumes stone and timber to stay standing - a permanent sink scaled by GEOGRAPHY rather than by population, which is a shape none of the other channels has. Second-order and wanted: it gives reach a running cost, so extending the network becomes a decision rather than a ratchet. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into LOGISTICS.md; the design register in MARKETS.md points at it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Government satellite launches - the tenth budget line, and space goods' first real buyer
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'add endpoints for space goods in government issued satellite launches'. Design in NATIONS.md section A budget. THE MACHINERY EXISTS - nations hold a weighted budget over priority lines, run_national_budget has claim/transfer machinery, and strategic_reserve is already a goods-buying line that no consumer claims on. THE WORK: a tenth line, space_programme, buying spacecraft_components and propellant through the BL-350 procurement seam (never on the open market - that is strategic_reserve's own rule). APPEND-ONLY: the weight vector is indexed by the enum and serialised, so the line goes last. Why it is worth more than a sink: state demand arrives in LUMPS and follows a weight a rival can lobby to move, so it is worth playing politics over rather than merely scaling into. ALSO OWNS spacecraft_components (BL-648's measurement, 2026-08-26): the guard's red list came back with ELEVEN goods, not the ten expected, and the eleventh is this one. Its exemption claimed BL-350 procurement, but procurement is a resource-agnostic TRANSFER between two corps' pools - it moves goods without consuming them, and admitting it as an injector would substantiate the entire roster at once. src/world contains no militia, and corp_ai.cpp says outright that the scorer does not emit those verbs today, so nothing automatic buys it. This line is its first real buyer.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Research consumes goods, not only credits
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26: 'perhaps we could make research consume alternate goods as well'. Design written into RESEARCH.md. It gives the TOP of the production chain a buyer and turns the tech ladder into an economic decision rather than a free accumulator only time gates. Two properties: the basket is era-banded like every other, and a shortfall SLOWS research rather than voiding it (the same shape every goods draw takes). BLOCKED BY DESIGN on BL-619 (research system), which is a session with Ben - the rates, and whether the draw sits on the university or on the nation's budget lines, belong to that session rather than being settled ahead of it.

items.author: Ben
items.title: A battle consumes what it fires - conflict as a demand shock
items.design: The conflict demand channel (MARKETS.md section Demand channels). MEASURED: ordnance is priced at 43.00, near the top of the ancient roster, and its only draw is a per-head upkeep rate that BL-635's rescale took to 0.0035 - effectively nil. So the roster's most valuable military good has no buyer. THE WORK: a battle draws ordnance in proportion to what it commits, against the owner's pool, deterministically. WHY IT IS THE MOST INTERESTING OF THE EIGHT: it is the only channel that couples the game's two pillars - it makes Conflict move Trade, so a war somewhere else is a price signal here. OWED: this item writes its paragraph into MILITARY.md.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Tobacco, spices, coffee and furs get the buyer they were authored for
items.design: MEASURED: four endemic goods are on the roster, extractable, priced - and wanted by nothing at all, in any band. They pass the orphan check by naming 'mercantile demand', which BL-648 shows does not exist. THE WORK: a household demand that scales with WEALTH rather than headcount, flavoured by NATIONAL CHARACTER so different nations crave different luxuries. That asymmetry is the design, not a detail: it makes the trade route directional by construction - extract where it grows, sell where the money is - which is the most Trade-shaped channel of the eight and the one that most directly serves the pillar. Note it is also the first demand whose SIZE is a function of prosperity, so it rewards a player who has made somewhere rich.

items.title: Finish the dissolution walk - ground follows the firm, and hoist the duplicated HQ rule
items.author: Ben
items.design: Two loose ends the wave-2 review barrier found in BL-628, neither a defect today. (1) world::province_holder takes a CORP id via battle_system.cpp's field_held_by, and dissolve_into's inventory does not carry it. Entity ids are monotonic with no recycling, so a stale holder is inert rather than aliasing - but R4's wording is 'no dangling reference survives', and ground is PROPERTY, so it TRANSFERS. Now written into FINANCE.md's three-way rule, which also gained a fourth outcome, KEEP, for the historical record - history is not property and is never rewritten, which is the one place a reference to the erased corp survives on purpose. Extend the harness fixture to hold a province, since it currently never constructs one. (2) recompute_hq in corp_command.cpp DUPLICATES designate_hq/corp_home_body from corporation_generation.cpp, including kProjectedReachUnits = 2.5f - unavoidable at authoring because another slice owned that file in the same wave. Both have landed; the review verified them line-for-line identical. Hoist to a shared seam so they cannot drift.

items.title: charter_reach is computed at generation and silently zeroed on load
items.author: Ben
items.design: Found by the wave-2 review barrier. BL-638 added settlement_state::charter (a charter_reach), and w_settlement/r_settlement do not carry it. The omission is SYMMETRIC so the stream stays consistent and no version bump is owed - it is not a corruption bug. It is a LATENT one: the field is silently zeroed on load, which is benign only while the sole readers are generate_corporations and its harness, both of which run before any save exists. It becomes wrong the moment BL-627 (profitability ledger), BL-629 (rival acquisition) or the generation ledger reads charter off a LOADED world - and it will read as 'this world has no charter' rather than as an error. TWO HONEST ROUTES, pick one and say why: serialise it (a version bump, claimed through next_save_version.js), or RECOMPUTE it on load from the ladder it is derived from, which costs no format change and cannot drift from its source. The second is probably right, since charter_reach is a pure function of already-serialised state.

items.title: A demand injector that cannot price a basket entry must SAY SO, not skip it
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE MECHANISM THAT MADE TWO SEPARATE BUGS INVISIBLE ON THE SAME DAY, which is why it is an item rather than a note. inject_population_demand and inject_background_demand both SKIP a basket entry whose resource carries no market base price - silently, with no warning and no row anywhere. Consequences observed 2026-08-26: (1) BL-649's census read as having no background demand at all on its first run, and (2) tools/verify/spawn_solvency.cpp - whose own header says it loads world_gen.lua and did not - measured BL-635's entire spawn diagnosis in a world where background demand did not exist. Neither failed. Both just quietly answered a question about a different world. THE WORK: an injector that cannot price a basket entry must report it - a named diagnostic on the first occurrence, and a harness row that FAILS on a basket naming an unpriced good, since that combination is always either a missing script or an authoring error and is never intended. A basket entry is a STATEMENT that somebody wants the good; silently dropping it turns a design statement into a no-op. Cheap, and it protects every measurement the rest of Sprint 21 depends on.

items.title: The eighth field - a return sees the whole quarter, not just the money loop
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben's ruling, 2026-08-26, on NR-655/NR-668 - option A of the three-way fork, and the measurement that forced it: a firm earning through mercenary contracts files a trailing_net IDENTICAL to a firm that earns nothing there, so BL-628's buyout undervalues it by exactly 640 credits (k 8.0 x the 80/quarter the record cannot see). Design in FINANCE.md section The eighth field. THE WORK: add `other` to quarterly_return = the whole-tick balance delta minus the money-loop net, and MOVE THE FILING from the end of apply_budget to after the tick's last balance mover - which is the part that needs care, since apply_budget does not own the tick and the headless harnesses call it directly. Then re-point corp_trailing_net at the mean of (net + other) so the buyout prices off the whole quarter. THREE PROPERTIES TO ASSERT: the seven flows still explain `net` unchanged; net+other telescopes EXACTLY over a run (the retain property extended from one function to the whole tick); and BL-628's own harness row that currently PINS the 640-credit blindness must be re-specified to pin the closure instead - do not delete it, invert it. `other` is deliberately NOT itemised: split into named lines it becomes a second budget breakdown competing with corp_budget, and the reason there is one accounting authority is that two of them disagree. Versions the save format.

items.title: A short pool buys on the market, up to a reservation ceiling
items.author: Ben
items.design: THE BLOCKER UNDER BL-641, AND PROBABLY UNDER FOUR MORE CHANNELS. Measured 2026-08-26: with building upkeep rates on, operating firms went 227 -> 19, because the goods drawn are produced 0.0 in band and a POOL DRAW never reaches market_component::demand - so the want never becomes a price, no rival scores the building that would supply it, and the sink starves itself. run_construction and run_processing already bid; run_unit_upkeep does not and carries the same latent defect. DESIGN-OWED, and the open question is Ben's because it widens FINANCE.md: should a goods draw place real demand on the market when the pool is short - and if so, does it BUY (spending credits, which makes upkeep a market participant) or merely SIGNAL (raising price without a transaction, which is cheaper but invents demand nobody pays for)? The first is coherent and expensive; the second is a thumb on the scale and should probably be refused on the same grounds the project refuses clamps. Until this is settled, BL-641's rates stay at 0.0 and every remaining channel (BL-643 infrastructure, BL-644 state, BL-645 research, BL-646 conflict) should be checked against property 3 before it is built, not after. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-08-26): 'Buy on the market, but at a threshold, buying is not allowed. This goes hand in hand with maximum and minimum prices for goods.' And ONE RULE FOR EVERY GOODS DRAW - unit upkeep takes the same shape, not a second one. Written into MARKETS.md section Settled: a short pool BUYS, up to a reservation ceiling. THE WORK: a short pool bids the shortfall into market_component::demand and pays for what it gets; above the ceiling it does not bid at all and the existing shortfall rule weakens the building (or unit) instead. The ceiling is authored in the PRICE BAND family beside floor_mult/ceil_mult, not in upkeep - it is a statement about what a good is worth paying, not about who is buying - and its value is MEASURED against the census and the operating-firm count, never guessed. It is the exact mirror of BL-386's seller-side floor_price: both sides may decline a trade, neither may dictate one. Turning BL-641's rates non-zero is gated on this landing.

items.title: Decide what actually shapes background density - the ratio, or the per-resource cap
items.author: Ben
items.design: Raised by BL-655's measurement and by its novelty flag. Pass 6 is documented as stopping on a 0.90 production/demand ratio, described as 'an emergent measurement rather than an injected clearing constant' and 'a stop condition, not a firm-count budget'. MEASURED: the ratio NEVER BINDS on the worlds we generate. `per_resource_firm_cap = 8` binds on every demanded resource, so the count is exactly specialists + 8 x basket breadth - which reproduced 104, 64 and 56 corps exactly across three configurations. Its own comment still says 'provisional - measure, then pin'. The doc has been corrected to describe what the code does; what is OPEN is which behaviour is wanted. THREE READINGS: (a) the cap is the real design and the ratio is dead weight - pin the cap deliberately, say density is breadth-driven, and delete the ratio; (b) the ratio is the real design and the cap is an emergency brake set too low - raise it until the ratio binds, which restores the 'calibrated, not authored' property the doc claims; (c) both, with the cap as a genuine guard against a pathological basket. Note the consequence either way: under (a) density becomes a function of how many DIFFERENT goods are wanted, so every demand channel Sprint 21 adds moves the world's size - which may be a feature.

items.title: A firm underwater long enough exits - give interest the consequence it is supposed to have
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED 2026-08-26 from Ben's own observation of the live build. Of 12 seeds, 3 clear with ZERO interest; the 9 that fail all dipped negative once and interest is then 43-60% of their whole loss, against an operating gap of only -24 to -40 cr/qtr. 1.02^80 = 4.9x over the warm start. The rate is not the defect - components.hpp's 'no insolvency consequence' is. A firm that would have died in year three trades for twenty and is handed to the player as wreckage. THE WORK: a firm underwater for N consecutive quarters EXITS - dissolved, or absorbed via BL-628's dissolve_into, which already moves holdings, pools, balance and returns and cancels the promises nobody is left to keep. N and the trigger are authored in economy.lua and MEASURED, not picked. DESIGN-OWED on three questions that are Ben's: (1) dissolve or absorb - absorption by a solvent neighbour is richer and reuses the buyout path, dissolution is simpler and leaves ground free; (2) does this run IN PLAY as well as in the pre-game, i.e. can the player's own corp fail - NR-670 already ruled a rival may not BUY the player out, and this is a different question about the player failing on their own account; (3) what happens to the ground and the workforce - a dissolved firm's tiles should probably become available rather than stay held. EXPECTED CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is priority A: the field at seat time becomes self-selected for viability, so BL-630's shortlist floor should start being met instead of falling through to its fallback on 23 of 24 seeds.

items.title: The solvency gate tests the price, not the position after the debt transfers
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED by BL-634, which found it by taking its own brief's gate literally. The acquisition price is max(0, book_value + k x trailing_net + balance) and the balance term is SIGNED, so a deeply indebted firm's negative cash cancels its book value, the sum goes below zero, and the floor hands it over FREE. On 5 of 8 seeds the cheapest buyable firm cost exactly 0 cr. The dissolution rule then transfers the debt at face value: one seed took on -13,358 cr for nothing, and 3 of 8 buyers that bought the cheapest firm were sunk by it. THE FLOOR IS NOT THE BUG - a worthless firm is worth nothing, and NR-648's reasoning stands. The bug is that the SOLVENCY GATE READS THE PRICE rather than the buyer's balance AFTER the transfer, which is the same shape as the non-finite-price bug BL-628 caught in its own code: a check applied to the wrong quantity. THE WORK: gate on the post-acquisition position, so a corp cannot be handed a liability it could never have chosen to take on. Then re-run acquisition_viability's --target cheapest sweep, where 'still earning after' should go 5/8 -> 8/8. Note the harness already measures BOTH gates and its --target flag exists for exactly this comparison.

items.title: Population lens: regional heatmap with harder scaling, not a per-tile mark
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "Population: Let's see what this looks like as a heatmap with more extreme scaling. This way we should be able to see population regionally, not just on each tile."

Today the lens draws "per-tile value marks, workforce efficiency" (LENSES.md routing table) - a per-tile read, which is why a region of moderate population and a region of none look similar at whole-planet zoom. Two changes: a continuous heatmap fill rather than discrete marks, and a scaling curve steep enough that regional differences separate instead of compressing into the middle of the ramp.

EXPLICITLY AN EXPERIMENT, in Ben's own framing - "let's see what this looks like". The deliverable is a capture to rule on, not a settled design; expect a second pass on the curve. Worth measuring the actual population distribution first so the curve is fitted to the data rather than guessed - the same discipline BL-649's census brought to demand.

items.title: Scarcity lens: drop the dead Opportunity code, reuse its glyph, render market scarcity per resource
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "I support changing opportunity to scarcity. Drop the old code, reuse the glyph, and render market scarcity per resource."

READ AS: the lens KEEPS the name Scarcity - the earlier idea of renaming it to Opportunity is dropped - while the retired Opportunity lens's leftovers are deleted and its GLYPH is reused for Scarcity. Recorded explicitly because the instruction can be read in both directions, and because the session had just flagged that Opportunity is a name BL-604 retired; if this reading is wrong it is a one-line revert.

WHY A GLYPH MATTERS HERE: Scarcity is keyboard-cycle only, which is why Ben listed it among the lenses needing glyphs. icons::opportunity survives in src/ui/icons.{hpp,cpp} with no caller since BL-604, so the mark exists and is unused - reusing it costs nothing and lets Scarcity earn a strip slot, since LENSES.md's rule is that an on-screen lens carries one distinct glyph.

Also dead and worth removing in the same sweep, though Ben named only Opportunity: icons::country (BL-601) and icons::production (BL-604), neither of which has a caller.

The behaviour half - "render market scarcity per resource" - may already hold: the lens draws "per-market shortfall blocks + key" keyed to the selected resource, and the 2026-08-28 sweep captured scarcity_lens_full_iron and _steel. Confirm before changing anything; the glyph may be the whole of the real work.

items.title: Give every strip-eligible lens a distinct glyph (Company; Supply, Supply-routes, Reach deferred)
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "It looks like we need to add glyphs for scarcity, supply, supply-routes, and reach."

WHAT REMAINS LIVE HERE IS THE COMPANY LENS, added 2026-08-28. It borrows icons::corporation while keyboard-only, on the precedent Reach and Supply-routes set. It cannot join the on-screen strip until it has its own mark, because Corp would be its immediate neighbour and LENSES.md forbids two strip neighbours sharing a glyph. A company is a background firm, so the mark wants to read as smaller/plural against the corporation's single solid form.

Three glyphs are dead and free to cannibalise: icons::country, icons::opportunity (claimed by BL-662), icons::production.

items.title: The Diplomacy ledger becomes corporations grouped by stance - Allies, Neutral, Rival
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29, on the slot-8 all-corporations table: "we should condense this to show corporations, and arrange it for Allies, Neutral, and Rival." And, splitting the surface in two: "This ledger is not quite the right place for companies, as they are less so diplomatic entities, and instead options to buy."

THE CONDENSE IS THE FIX, and it is a population change before it is a layout one. The table today lists EVERY corporation_component in the world - 88 rows on the fixture, measured 2026-08-29 from its own footer. Since the 2026-08-28 glossary split a Corporation is the player and its rivals and a Company is a background firm, so ~80 of those 88 rows are companies standing in a diplomatic surface. Filtering to !is_background is what takes the surface from 88 rows to a handful, and it is Ben's sentence read literally rather than a layout trick.

THREE GROUPS, NOT A COLUMN. Allies / Neutral / Rival become collapsing sections and the Stance COLUMN goes: under the grouping the column would restate its own heading on every row. Reach goes too - it reads "1 bodies" on all 88 rows on the fixture, a column that has never discriminated - and Share goes with it (0% or 1% on almost every row, and the acquisition surface takes over the financial read; see BL-627). What is left is the firm's NAME, which is the thing the surface has never been able to show.

THAT FIXES NR-709 AT THIS SITE. corporation_panel.cpp declares Reach/Capital/Share at WidthFixed 62 and Stance at WidthFixed 220 - 406 px of fixed width inside a ~358 px fold-out column - so the one WidthStretch column, the name, absorbs the whole overflow and collapses to a single glyph (NR-705). Deleting three of the five columns removes the starvation rather than papering over it. The sibling instance in the Economy panel Markets view is NOT in scope here and stays on NR-709.

GROUP MEMBERSHIP reads the existing tables and invents no predicate: Allies from are_friends (symmetric), Rival from is_hostile in EITHER direction, Neutral is the remainder. Hostility is directed (RELATIONS.md § Stance), so a Rival row must say WHICH WAY - a corp the player declared against and a corp that declared against the player are not the same situation, and RELATIONS.md already settles that a declaration against the player is signalled (Ben, 2026-08-22). Do not collapse the two behind one stance_between() accessor; the doc names that as a thing never to do.

THE STANCE PRESSES STAY - they are the only route to the four stance verbs, and BL-449 (stance needs a surface) has no other host. They move out of a 220 px column into the row's own action affordance. Declare Hostile keeps its confirm ("Dissolves any friendship. Not unilaterally reversible."); Offer / Accept Friendship and Return to Neutral keep their current behaviour. A press that changes stance MOVES THE ROW BETWEEN GROUPS, which is the grouping earning its place.

CAPITAL stays and keeps the disclosure rule exactly (FINANCE.md § Disclosure): exact for a public firm, a dash for a private or closed one, exact always for the player's own row. A dash means the firm does not file, never that the player has not earned it. No bands - they are retired.

OPEN, and Ben's: whether the three group headings carry a count, and whether an empty group renders as a heading with "none" or is omitted. Recommend a count on the heading and an explicit empty state, since Allies will usually be empty at campaign start and an omitted section reads as a missing feature.

RELATIONSHIP TO BL-639 (corp panel column budget): this item SUPERSEDES it, and both must not be built. BL-639 is Ben's 2026-08-26 filing of the same defect at the same site, proposing to re-budget five columns against shell_column_width. Deleting three of the five is the stronger fix and is what the 2026-08-29 instruction asks for. BL-639 is annotated in place and left for Ben to close.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Merged and verified in the main session, not taken on the agent report: BUILD_OK, diplomacy_groups 12/12, sibling corp_disclosure green. Measured 88 corporations -> 80 background -> 8 rows drawn. The ImGui table is gone entirely; rows are manual and every extent derives from the live content region, so NR-709 cannot recur here by the same mechanism. Ben ratified the group names Friends / Hostile / Neutral over his own first wording, on the agent argument that the glossary models hostility and friendship with no alliance relation, and that rival already means any non-player corp. THE LIVE-CLICK REQUIREMENT ROW IS PENDING - synthesised presses through ImGui hit-test only.

items.title: A new ledger for buying companies - Purchasable and Possible, with a sortable fold-out
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "we need a new ledger for purchasing companies... We can remove both the stance and reach columns, and collapse the 'share' mechanic, and just use outright purchasing. So we can have two dropdowns, one for 'purchasable' (can afford), and 'possible' (can't afford)."

THE SURFACE. Two collapsing groups over the buyable field: PURCHASABLE (acquisition price <= the player corp's balance) and POSSIBLE (priced, but not affordable today). The same disclosure idiom as everywhere else - a firm that does not file does not appear at all, because it cannot be priced. Per row: the firm's name and its price. The buy press sits on Purchasable rows only; a Possible row shows the price and no press, which is the whole point of the second group.

NO STANCE, NO REACH, NO SHARE. Those three columns belong to the diplomatic read (BL-674) and this surface is not that. "Collapse the share mechanic and just use outright purchasing" is already the settled model rather than a change: FINANCE.md § Whole-firm acquisition and GLOSSARY § Corporation both say ownership moves WHOLE, by buyout, with no fractional stake, no share count and no controlling-holder threshold. So this ledger asks the seam for nothing new.

IT USES THE EXISTING VERB UNCHANGED. corp_verb::buy_corporation already prices at max(0, book_value + k_acquisition_multiple x trailing_net + balance) and already gates on: not the player, publicly_held, and has actually filed. Note what that gate does NOT say - it does not test is_background. So the buyable field is every public filed firm, which in practice is overwhelmingly background COMPANIES because rivals are few. Ben's framing describes that population; it is not a new gate, and none should be added.

MEASURE BEFORE BUILDING THE LAYOUT, and treat the number as capable of overturning the design. On the fixture most firms showed a dash for Capital, i.e. are not public, so the two groups may be nearly empty at campaign start. FIRST TASK: report how many firms are public-and-filed, what their prices are, and how many fall each side of the player's balance over several seeds. tools/verify/acquisition_viability.cpp (BL-634) already measures the buy side and is the place to extend rather than a fresh harness. If the honest answer is "two firms, both unaffordable", say so and bring it back - do not pad the surface to look busy.

THE FOLD-OUT IS BL-627, not a second design. Ben: "This ledger should have a fold out option which displays a full table, sortable by type, end resource, input resource, profit... And any other useful fields." That is the profitability ledger BL-627 has been design-owed for since Sprint 20, and BL-627 is already described as "the host of the buyout press". It takes the BL-214 full-canvas disclosure idiom the Corporation dashboard already uses - which is, on the evidence of the 2026-08-29 capture pass, the best-reading surface in the whole ledger family and the one the others should be measured against.

REACHABILITY, and the one open call. The surface is wired first as the COMPANY-LENS click destination, replacing the placeholder BL-666 left there - a Company-lens press is literally "I am looking at a firm I might buy", so the routing is already right. WHETHER IT ALSO EARNS A NAV-RAIL SLOT IS BEN'S CALL and is deliberately not assumed here: MENU.md curates thirteen slots and a fourteenth is a shell change, not a ledger change. Build the ledger reachable from the lens; wire the rail slot when Ben names one. Recorded as an open call rather than a default so the rail is not grown by accident.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. Merged and verified in the main session: BUILD_OK, acquisitions_ledger 20/20, lens_one_tier 38/38 after its company assertion was updated to the new destination. Nav slot 5, tab_count 13->14 (returned to 13 by BL-676), Company-lens click destination replacing the BL-666 placeholder. THE MEASUREMENT IS THE RESULT WORTH KEEPING: the public-and-filed field is 1-3 firms per seed, mean 1.6, against mean 84.8 closed - and filing excluded ZERO firms on every seed, so ownership class is the only binding gate. The ledger states its own field size on its face rather than letting one row read as a defect. THE LIVE-CLICK REQUIREMENT ROW IS PENDING.

items.title: Retire the Economy panel outright, and Construction takes slot 3
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29, after looking at all three of its views: "Looking at the workforce ledger, we can actually drop it entirely. Reorder construction to slot 3, and we can shove everything else up one slot. So for this ledger, just delete all relevant code, since we don't need to use it, and its contents are better placed elsewhere."

A DELETION, NOT A DEPRECATION. The panel's own doc had carried "does Economy survive as a distinct surface?" as its lead question since the ledger-mockup pass, and answered it with option (B), fold it away. This is that call taken. Every file below loses its Economy references; economy_panel.cpp and .hpp go entirely.

WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG AND WHY IT DOES NOT NOW. The 2026-08-29 capture pass measured all three views, and each one turned out to be answered better somewhere else. Corps printed a rival balance ranking that BL-674 (diplomacy by stance) and BL-627 (profitability ledger) now own between them - and printed it with exact figures, which the competitor-visibility rule forbids. Markets duplicated the Market ledger, having lost its own resource-name column to the same starved-stretch-column defect as NR-709. Holdings itemised every rival corporation's stockpile to the decimal.

SO THE DELETION RESOLVES NR-711 OUTRIGHT. That entry filed the pools leak as live, documented and unowned - the item its own doc named as the fix, BL-482, no longer exists in the backlog. Deleting the surface removes the breach rather than redacting it, which is the stronger outcome. Close NR-711 against this item.

WHAT DOES NOT GET DELETED WITH IT: the labour read. The Workforce view was the one genuinely aggregate-only thing on the panel, and BL-677 (the labour read has no home) carries it out so the finding is not lost with the surface that displayed it wrongly.

THE RAIL, after this and after BL-675 inserted Acquisitions above Market. Thirteen slots again - one added, one removed:
  1 Corporation overview | 2 Budget | 3 Construction | 4 Research | 5 Acquisitions | 6 Market | 7 Corp. Strategy | 8 Diplomacy | 9 History | 10 Generation | 11 AI decisions | 12 Strategy | 13 Contracts
Construction moves from 7 to 3; Research, Acquisitions and Market keep their numbers; everything from Corp. Strategy down shifts up one. `tab_count` returns to 13.

MENU.md's STATED SHAPE CHANGES AND MUST BE REWRITTEN, not left to drift. It describes nine curated player slots, a three-slot developer tail, and one further player-system slot appended after it. After this the curated set is NINE again (Acquisitions in, Workforce out), the tail is 10-12, and Contracts is 13 - which is the shape the file already describes, reached by a different route. It also says three slots host a provisional occupant; Workforce was one of the three, so that count drops to two.

NOT A SAVE-FORMAT CHANGE. `show_economy_panel` and `economy_view` are checked and are NOT serialised in src/core/save_game.cpp, so no envelope field moves and save_game_version does not bump. Confirm that before deleting rather than after - NR-708 records that no envelope field has round-trip coverage and that read_save_game refuses the whole file on a version mismatch.

TWO TRAPS IN THE VERIFY LAYER, both of which will fail a run if missed. `verify.econ_step` OPENS THE ECONOMY PANEL as a side effect - scripts/verify/lib.lua's stage_ui_fixture closes it again explicitly and says so in a comment - so the side effect goes with the panel and that workaround goes with it. And shell_pass.lua, ledger_pass.lua and lib.lua all name "economy" in their panel lists.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. The agent completed its edits and STALLED during its own verification re-run; the main session committed the work from its worktree and did the verification, which is where that duty sat anyway. 922 deletions across 85 files. economy_panel.cpp/.hpp, economy.md, economy_panel.lua and economy_panel_refit.lua are gone; show_economy_panel and economy_view are out of ui_state, and neither was serialised, so no envelope field moved and save_game_version did NOT bump. The rail is thirteen slots again, read case by case out of nav_pane.cpp: 1 Corporation overview, 2 Budget, 3 Construction, 4 Research, 5 Acquisitions, 6 Market, 7 Corp. Strategy, 8 Diplomacy, 9 History, 10 Generation, 11 AI decisions, 12 Strategy, 13 Contracts. Verified: BUILD_OK, shell_pass green, diplomacy_groups 12/12, acquisitions_ledger 20/20, lens_one_tier 38/38. Slot 8 also stopped being provisional - its tooltip and its standing comment both still described the balance table BL-674 replaced, and the rail was teaching the wrong subject. NR-711 (economy panel pools leak) is resolved BY DELETION rather than by redaction. NR-716 filed: shell_pass reaches ledgers by name and never presses a rail slot, so it could not have caught a bad renumber - the mapping was confirmed by reading, which is not a check.

items.title: The labour read has no home, and wage competition is invisible
items.author: Claude
items.design:
FILED SO A FINDING IS NOT DELETED ALONG WITH THE SURFACE THAT DISPLAYED IT WRONGLY. BL-676 retires the Economy panel on Ben's 2026-08-29 call. Two of its three views were duplicates and one was a visibility breach, but the Workforce view was answering a real question badly rather than answering a redundant one - and after the deletion nothing answers it at all.

WHAT THE CAPTURE PASS MEASURED. The workforce table drew eighteen rows and every single one read "82% (labour short)". The panel's own doc had warned the mock fixture was uniform at 85% and said explicitly: verify against the live sim, not the CSV. Verified against the live sim - it is uniform there too.

AND IT IS NOT A BUG. `report.workforce_contention` is the POOL-LEVEL min(1, supply/demand) keyed (corp, body), and every corp in the fixture holds on one body, so one pool yields one number correctly repeated eighteen times. The view is not broken; it is showing a quantity that cannot vary in the situation it is shown in.

THE ACTUAL FINDING: BL-614 (wage competition) SUPERSEDED that scalar and nothing surfaces what replaced it. economy_system.cpp says so in terms - when a pool is contended the uniform proportional scalar no longer applies; scarce labour allocates building by building, offered wage descending (base_wage x (1 + wage_bid)), building id ascending on a tie, each granted up to its demand until the pool is spent. The marginal building takes a partial grant and those below it get nothing. The factor a building actually runs at is `report.building_labour[id]`, and the pool aggregate survives only as a reporting figure.

So there is a real mechanic here - bidding for scarce labour, and losing a building's shift to a rival who bid higher - and the only surface that ever mentioned labour rendered it as one number eighteen times. `building_labour[id]` is per building and varies; it is the quantity a player would act on.

DESIGN-OWED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED HERE. Where this lives is open and is Ben's: a section on the building Selection card (per-building, where the number's grain actually is), a view on the Corporation dashboard beside the existing Workforce roll-up card, or a surface of its own. What is settled is only that it has no home today and that the Budget ledger's Wages tier currently has no visible consequence anywhere.

items.title: Retire ownership closure for companies - every background firm is transparent and buyable
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29, ruling through the design form: retire closure for COMPANIES ONLY - every background firm is transparent and buyable. CORPORATIONS KEEP THEIR CLASS. He raised it while reading the profitability table: "Can you describe what closed means... closed seems to give no information. I might ask to retire closure, and ensure that all companies are 100% for sale and transparent. (But not corporations)."

WHAT PROMPTED IT, and it is worse than the column looked. `ownership_class` has three values and every consumer in the tree tests `!= publicly_held` - verify_api.cpp, acquisitions_ledger.cpp twice, corp_command.cpp's buy gate. NOTHING anywhere distinguishes `privately_held` from `closed`. It is a three-value enum doing a two-value job, and the third value exists only as a label in a column. Ben was offered the collapse to two values and DECLINED it, so the redundancy stays for now and is recorded rather than fixed - the enum is a serialised uint8_t and collapsing it is the one option in that form that touches the save envelope.

THE CHANGE. A background firm (`is_background`) is `publicly_held`, always. A corporation keeps the derivation it has - home region industrialisation timing and nation ideology, CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 2b.

DETERMINISM IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT. Apply the override AFTER the existing derivation rather than branching inside it, so the RNG stream is untouched and no downstream generation shifts. A background firm still consumes exactly the randomness it consumed before; only the stored value changes. If that cannot be done without moving the stream, stop and report rather than accepting the drift.

MEASURE THE CONSEQUENCE BEFORE CALLING IT DONE, because it is large and it is not a UI number. The buyable field goes from a mean of 1.6 firms per seed to roughly 85 (measured pre-change: 1.6 public, 1.6 private, 84.8 closed, of 88). AND RIVALS BUY TOO - `buy_corporation` is scored in corp_ai.cpp's candidate list under the solvency gate (FINANCE.md § Rivals buy too). Making 85 firms acquirable could let a rival snowball through acquisition in a way the economy has never been exercised against. Re-run `tools/verify/acquisition_viability.cpp` across its twelve seeds and report: how many acquisitions actually occur over a run, rival solvency before and after, and whether field holdings concentrate. If the economy degenerates, that is a finding for Ben, not something to tune away.

THE FICTION HAS TO FOLLOW. GLOSSARY § Ownership class currently says the class does two jobs and no others, for corporations generally. FINANCE.md § Disclosure and § Who may be bought both read as universal rules. All three need to say that the class applies to CORPORATIONS and that companies are open by construction - a background firm is part of the commercial population the player trades with, not a rival whose books are its own.

ONE KNOCK-ON TO FIX WHILE HERE: the `acquisitions_ledger_field` question_log entry's justification cites the measured field size ("one to three firms... because ownership class is overwhelmingly closed"). That becomes false the moment this lands. Re-measure and rewrite that clause; do not leave a settled entry citing a stale number, which is precisely the failure docs/ui/ledgers/_critic_notes.md exists to warn about.

items.title: A firm the player knows nothing about is not listed at all
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "operational fog should hide details. But that should be binary. If we don't know what a company does, then we don't know anything about it. If we do know, then we get all information." Ruling through the form: known = every field; unknown = THE ROW IS NOT LISTED AT ALL.

THE PROBLEM IT FIXES. The profitability table draws every corporation in the world and gates three operational columns (type, end resource, input resource) on disclosure, so 85 of 88 rows render as a name, the word "closed", and five dashes. The table is correct and almost entirely empty; the two readable rows are lost in it.

IT IS SMALLER THAN IT SOUNDS, and the reason is worth knowing before starting. There is NO fog term in this code at all. `discloses()` in acquisitions_ledger.cpp is already binary and reads ownership class alone - the graded band was retired in 2026-08-26. The per-column gate was an implementation choice layered on top of it, not a rule from any doc. So Ben's ruling is a FILTER, not a new predicate: list a row only where `discloses()` is true, and inside a listed row show every field unconditionally.

WHAT GOES: the whole dash apparatus on this surface - `disclosure_dash`, the absent-sorts-last comparators that exist only so a dashed cell sorts sanely, and the ownership column's reason-on-hover. None of it has a subject once undisclosed rows are gone. Delete it rather than leaving it unreachable.

WHAT STAYS, and do not conflate the two surfaces: the DIPLOMACY ledger (BL-674) still lists every corporation with a dash for Capital where the firm does not file. That is correct and unchanged - it is the relational read, and a rival you cannot price is still a rival you have a stance toward. This ruling is about the financial table only.

COMPOSES WITH BL-678 (companies are open), and the pair is the point. With closure retired for companies, every company discloses and is listed in full; a private or closed CORPORATION is simply absent from this table while still appearing under Diplomacy. Neither item needs the other to land, but the table only stops looking sparse when both have.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24. The agent was lost to an API error on its last step; the main session committed its worktree and did the verification. The profitability table now lists only disclosing firms and shows every field on a listed row - 88 rows of mostly dashes became 4 rows of real data. The dash apparatus is deleted rather than left unreachable. The surface states the rule on its own face: "A firm that does not file is not listed - if it discloses, every figure is here." TWO GENUINE ABSENCES SURVIVE AND ARE CORRECTLY DISTINGUISHED FROM DISCLOSURE: an extraction firm has no input resource, and the player cannot be sold a price for itself. Those are facts about the row, not things withheld, and the check asserts them separately. Verified: BUILD_OK, 81 assertions pass, 0 fail.

items.title: Filter the profitability table by end resource, input resource and body
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-29: "Perhaps we should add filtering to the table, since closed seems to give no information." Ruling through the form, he chose THREE filters and declined four others: BY END RESOURCE, BY INPUT RESOURCE, BY BODY.

WHAT HE DECLINED, and why the omissions are coherent rather than arbitrary. "Affordable only" and "Profitable only" were offered and not taken - the Purchasable / Possible split in the ledger above already answers affordability, and a profit sort answers the other. "Hide the unknown" was offered and not taken because his fog ruling (BL-679) removes unknown rows entirely, so the filter would have no subject. "Name search" was not taken. Do not add any of the four back.

ALL THREE FILTERS ARE SUPPLY-CHAIN QUESTIONS, which is the reading that should drive the implementation. End resource and input resource together let a player ask "who makes the thing I need" and "who competes with me for the input I buy" - the two questions that make buying a firm a strategic act rather than a purchase. Body scopes it to where the player can actually reach.

The filters are CROSS-CUTTING SELECTORS, not views, so they are exempt from the toggle rule (io-standing-rules.md § Toggle rule) exactly as the Market ledger's Body and Market combos are.

Populate each filter from the rows actually present rather than from the full resource registry - a filter offering forty goods where the visible field holds four is a worse surface than no filter. Combine as AND across the three, and say so on the surface when a combination yields nothing, rather than drawing an empty table.
items.summary: Landed 2026-08-29, Sprint 24, alongside BL-679 (binary fog listing). Three cross-cutting selectors - end resource, input resource, body - populated from the drawn rows rather than the resource registry, combining as AND. The four filters Ben declined were not added. THE CHECK CRASHED WHEN FIRST RUN HERE and had never executed: it called table.sort, and the verify Lua sandbox opens no table library - lib.lua carries a hand-written insertion sort for exactly this reason and says so. Fixed by sorting by hand, which made the A8/A9 assertions reachable for the first time. A9 drives the combos through real clicks. HONEST RESULT WORTH KEEPING: the body filter swept 1 option and narrowed nothing, because every disclosing firm on the fixture sits on one body. Reported rather than hidden; it will discriminate once BL-678 (companies are open) widens the field.
